input.quote: are the property of Company to the extent that such Works were created by Contractor for Company over a time period for which Company has been invoiced and said invoice has been paid.
input.rationale: Section 4(a) purports to vest the Works in Company but only "to the extent" they were created in a period that has been invoiced and paid, with no present assignment and no interim licence. Title is therefore fragmented invoice-by-invoice, and any unbilled, unpaid or disputed period leaves the work product we commissioned owned by Contractor with no rights back to us — below even the fallback, which requires a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables. Section 4(d) compounds this by deferring our right to modify the software until payment in full. The document also contains no statement that Company retains ownership of its own data and pre-existing materials (Section 8 treats it only as confidential information). Contractor's retention of its background tools and know-how under 4(b) and the perpetual, royalty-free, sublicensable licence-back in 4(c) are acceptable and unchanged; the licence-back's silence on irrevocability is noted only, not flagged. Redline makes the Works vest by present assignment on creation and adds a Customer Data/materials ownership sentence.

proposal.summary: Make Works vest in Company by present assignment on creation (not conditioned on invoicing/payment) and confirm Company retains ownership of its own data and materials.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need the work product we commission to vest in us on creation by present assignment rather than only for periods already invoiced and paid, and we cannot leave our own data and pre-existing materials unaddressed. Contractor's background IP and its licence-back under 4(b) and 4(c) are unchanged; if helpful, we can pair this with prompt-payment or suspension remedies elsewhere.

ops.oldText: are the property of Company to the extent that such Works were created by Contractor for Company over a time period for which Company has been invoiced and said invoice has been paid.
ops.newText: are the property of Company, and Contractor hereby irrevocably assigns to Company all right, title and interest in and to the Works upon creation, whether or not any invoice relating to such Works has then been issued or paid. Company retains all right, title and interest in and to all data, materials and intellectual property provided or made available by Company or its users to Contractor, and nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers any such rights to Contractor.
